To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Young APP23 mice overexpressing APP with the Swedish mutation display altered novelty-seeking behavior before the age and plaque onset, (2) siRNAs targeting APP can be used to reduce expression of human APP in the brain of APP mice, (3) APP23 mice infused with siRNA targeting APP display a normal exploratory phenotype in a novel environment.

(1) APP23 mice display an increased exploratory activity when placed in a new environment; (2) this phenotype is reversed by siRNAs targeted against APP; and (3) the reversal of the behavioral phenotype is not linked to plaque formation.
APP23 transgenic mouse model of Alzheimer's disease shows altered novelty-seeking behavior before plaque formation, which is fully reversed by siRNA targeted against human APP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of siRNA as an effective treatment for Alzheimer's disease and other neurodegenerative diseases.
the direct role of APP and its products in behavioral abnormalities associated with Alzheimer's disease and the development of novel therapeutic strategies for this disorder.
the role of APP and its products in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
APP overexpression in the APP23 mouse model of AD leads to an increase in exploratory activity in a novel environment that is reversed by siRNAs targeting APP.
APP23 transgenic mouse model is a useful tool for investigating the effects of APP and its derivative on the central nervous system.
APP and its derivatives have an important role in the regulation of novelty seeking behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
APP and its derivatives may play a role in novelty seeking behavior and that this role is separable from the role of APP in plaque deposition.
we have demonstrated for the first time, using siRNA, that excessive APP and its derivatives, causes hyperactivity and increased exploration in a novel environment.
APP and/or its fragments are necessary for a normal exploratory behavior in mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
APP and/or its products are implicated in a behavioral phenotype that is independent of amyloid plaques.
the behavioral phenotype in APP mice is not due to plaque deposits, but is due to the overexpression of APP.
